Whether you desire coastal or country locations, full-on fun or a relaxing time with loved ones, each resort is alive with character and atmosphere, and specially crafted to suit your needs. 
Each Away Resorts park makes the most of its unique surroundings and individual appeal. Explore the New Forest at Sandy Balls, go wakeboarding at Tattershall Lakes, hit the golf course at Appletree or enjoy a bucket-and-spade family holiday at Beachcomber, all in Lincolnshire. Sample the local cuisine at Mersea Island, kick back and relax at Barmouth Bay or enjoy a seaside break at Golden Sands, both in Wales. Or why not hit the waves at our 5 Cornish beauties. Discover our new-look Hayling Island gem, Mill Rythe or enjoy a seaside holiday like no other at at one of our 4 parks on the glorious Isle of Wight… the choice really is all yours!
Many of our parks are jam-packed with fantastic facilities, from on-site restaurants and bars to indoor and outdoor swimming pools. As for entertainment and events– well, there is something to keep every member of the family grinning from ear to ear.  
Our team are on a mission; to make your break brilliant. Where your accommodation is off-the-scale amazing and new experiences await at every turn. A holiday to create “remember when we did that?” moments that will last a lifetime. So, are you ready to fall in love with a new type of holiday?
title: Would have had five stars however when…
review: Would have had five stars however when booking a 4 night break on 20th November we arrived to find out neither the small clubhouse or indoor swimming pool were open the whole stay we were there and only opened Friday to Sunday.It was not a discounted price but should have been notified facilities were closed.

title: Great place to stay,  just a couple of negatives
review: Accommodation, activities and the site itself we love. We’ve holidayed here a few times now and our kids love it! We stay in knightswood accomodation and it’s fantastic. The only things that let the place down are the dining facilities and the pools. Food in the pub and restaurant is not great quality at all! We’ve tried both every time we visit and it doesn’t get any better. The pools both need a refurb, kids still have a great time but both pools are really old. The changing rooms are dire!Other than this we love the place. Staff are friendly, great activities, beautiful calm surroundings and great accommodation.

title: Booked to stay at Freshwater
review: Booked to stay at Freshwater, IOW weekend 6th -8th Dec, then storm Darragh hit the whole country!  With national news advising everyone to not travel unless its essential, we rang Away Resorts on the Fri am of our holiday booking, to see if we could amend our booking to the following week. We spoke to Steve Dunn the custoner service manager for the company, who was so unhelpful! Would not alow any amendment, only if the weather forecast went to a red warning!! So we managed to get to the IOW and our holiday cottage, but we are now having a 6 hour delay waiting to find out if we can get a ferry home today!  Away Resorts and Steve Dunn need to review their customer service policy with regards to adverse weather conditions, and i suggest a course in good customer service management training for senior management... such a shame as the whole team at Freshwater were amazing, thank you

title: Disappointed as we’re not pet lovers …
review: St IvesFirst impressions of the site were very good, well maintained and looked after. We booked a Stargazer with a sea view and hot tub. The caravan looked lovely with modern furnishings. Naively we weren’t aware the accommodation was pet friendly until we saw the neighbouring caravan had a dog. This explained the dog hairs on the sofas & floor and the dirty carpets in the hallway & bedrooms. It’s not nice to see a dog doing its business on the decking and then walk in & out a caravan. We also felt we couldn’t sit on the soft furniture in the restaurant area due to muddy footprints, dog hair and the smell of wet dog.Later the same day it was apparent there was a problem with the drainage in our caravan. We couldn’t use the en-suite and kept the door closed with the window open while we were in the caravan. When showering you could hear the water gurgling through the kitchen sink.For us, it’s a lesson learned and made us aware to check in future if the accommodation is pet friendly.

title: Just got back from weekend at…
review: Just got back from weekend at Tattleshall lakes, booked a superior lodge, dog friendly one the place needs a good clean, very Dusty, cob webs, dishwasher useless and dosent clean properly, shower leaking, toilet dosent flush very well, outside furniture covered in bird poo and no cushions for the metal set which we would probably have hire for £12 no towels have pay for them £12 no iron or iron board have to pay another £12. title: We rented a disabled lodge from Sandy…
review: We rented a disabled lodge from Sandy balls. The lodge was very old and tired looking . The lighting was very poor in the bedrooms prob due to it all being wooden inside. Some of the strip lights were not working in the bedrooms. Sofas had holes in the cushions . The wet room was fine apart from the radiators were all rusty . We only found out just before we were to depart that there was no internet which I think is very poor. And there was no phone signal either . The plus was we were near all the facilities so we had to go there to obtain internet or phone in an emergency .

title: Nice lodge, but don't expect wifi

Exclusive cabin was big and comfortable,well looked after hot tub, great decking area,   adequate kitchen equipment,  beds ok although 2ft6in tiny for adults. Lack of WiFi a massive issue: app for booking activities is useless without! And providing a smart tv is pointless...No phone signal either. Toilet flush was intermittent  and dishwasher didn't clean anything well- maintenance came out promptly but didn't resolve totally. Pool area nice although must get packed in summer , entertainment good, but small seating area  and VERY expensive bar!!! Food in restaurants also pricey.

title: Disappointed in Sandy Balls

Booked for 4 people but only 3 towel sets provided which seemed odd. Staff at arrival were a bit lack lustre and low on information. Pub food was poor for the price, although Aubrey's Kitchen was better, and wait staff there were very friendly. The location could have done with a bit more signage and information about forest walks etc as there is no phone signal anywhere in the village so difficult to look up (unless you sit in pub where there is free wifi).

title: Retallack Lakeside 110 Lodge
review: Just finished a 10 night stay at Retallack Resort. Our lodge was quite tired looking and the facilities could do with a freshen up. Lots of cobwebs indoors and outdoors was a surprise for start of oeak season. Plenty space and quiet lodge overlooking the lake. No welcome pack to help with local area or how to use the TV and hottub. We reported a leaking shower and patio doors not closing properly. Someone came to check both after a chaser, but neither fixed. We were promised prosecco and beer which never came. The onsite watersport activities were great and staff really friendly. We secured a good price for our stay, but would be disappointed with freshness if arriving later into July when price jumps.

title: Would rather stay in privately owned accommodation rather then Away Resorts accommodation
review: Been to the Tattershall Lakes park many of times before but it's always been at caravans that was privately owned, so this was the first time we have stayed in an Away Resorts accommodation.We chose a luxury lodge....didn't get any luxury though. Was supposed to be an 8 birth Lodge with the sofa bed, but was only set up for 6. Had to ask for the spare bedding to have covers, spare cutlery and glasses, only 6 chairs but apparently the site had no spares and they only suggestions was either eat sat on the sofa or eat in shifts. Very minimal cooking equipment like pans and trays. Would recommend you bring your own stuff if you want to cook.As we had a child with us we booked to see the shows and mrs claus kitchen, the show on the Saturday started earlier then on the ticket, ticket says 730pm start but it started at 7pm. Mrs claus kitchen was rushed, not very organised and for the price was pretty naff.

Ant infestation in master bedroom and ensuite. Responded to by professional 'ant man' but took forty eight hours to work consequently had to sleep on bed settee and single bed. Gasket round oven door lying in bottom of oven required a self fix as no-one from site turned up.Had lame apology and 20% discount offered for another holiday. Point is, none of this should happen in the first place, extremely bad management.

review: My experience with Love Holidays has been nothing short of a nightmare. I was forced to accept it to avoid losing more than £2,000.Overall:Love Holidays completely failed to provide proper support in both situations. They don’t care about their customers or their money. Once they’ve taken your payment, you’re on your own. Their service is slow, disorganized, and completely unreliable.I will never use Love Holidays again, and I strongly recommend others stay away if you want to avoid stress, financial loss, and ruined holidays.

review: The website was easy to navigate but didn’t appear to have a facility for providing extra information. I wanted to book a veggie meal for the flights but found no mechanism for doing so. I was directed to the chat but this turned out to be a useless bot that didn’t forward me to a human when it could not help.I eventually found a number and after a while got through to a helpful human being. But if TUI are going to save money by cutting back on any genuine chat service, be honest and say so rather than directing me to a bot and faqs that are no help.When I did get to speak to someone by ringing TUI they were very helpful.

description: Discover the world of TUI and your smile. Explore our holiday destinations and collections designed around you.
title: We booked xmas Rhine cruise  on TUI…
review: We booked xmas Rhine cruise  on TUI ISLA boat 23 dec to 30th .First error was flying into Frankfurt which may be the largest airport in Germany but is as we all know chaos at every level. Systems to get three different cruise customers to their boats was disorganised at best and once we reached our boat was told we could not access our cabin until 3pm .Because housekeeping had not checked them walking down down to our cabin it was clearly ready and cases had been delivered .We finally obtained our keys when two ladies were more insistent  than i was.As for checking cabin  shower room extractor fan  did not work one light was out and shower room cabinet door was falling off. The cabinet was fixed after four days with the guy saying sorry we have so many problems with the boat.Light and extractor fan never fixed. One day all toilets on the boat were shut down for half an hour and ladies toilet near reception was closed most of the week this had been mentioned on previous trip advisor reports.We like a number of people began to suffer bad smells coming from the shower drain. Plus only one heating vent ever worked in the cabin. Exercise bike in gym did not work .When questions were asked seems staff had been told to say check the app as no instructions on meal times ,entertainment in the cabin,No safety meeting which i thought was compulsory just a message on tv which had 9 channels three of which were in german, not many of them on the boat. Food was ok to good and our waiter in the rear restaurant worked so hard to fix any problem, but christmas day dinner was as disaster with TUI trying to be al a carte rather than serving a quality uk type .meal Tours and guides were fine and it would not take more than a professional manager running the boat to obtain a quality standard trip. Needless to say we shall not be using TUI again.

We managed to get to the gate in Dubai for connecting flight in time only to find out our tickets was cancelled while we was in the air on the flight from London.Both times we missed 1 day of our holiday. Airlines didn’t want to know. TUI not much better. Took them 6 months to reply to our complaint. Basically telling us they have nothing to do with it. Even flights are included in their package.Very disappointed as we purchased 8 package holidays in the last 4 years.

Two days earlier AA had announced that they would now be using terminal 5 . Enquired through TUI website it will be 5,So booked coach to 5. Another couple of days and web still saying it’s from 3. Just to be sure rang again and was told 3 was correct . ????? So now got to get from 5to 3. Both outgoing and incoming. Moral of the story do not believe what they tell you ?? Asked if I was interested in a taxi transfer to hotel . Asked the price £192. Was I buying the car ?? Or is the coach transfer going to be horrendous. This is before the holiday has even begun .warning you should take some beach shoes as their might be some rocky bits on the beach ?? Pristine white sandy beaches ? Apprehensive to say the least . description: Discover the world of TUI and your smile. Explore our holiday destinations and collections designed around you.
title: Poor Tui  rep experience
review: We were on a all inclusive holiday in Bavaro, Punta Cana, Dominican Republic for 10 nights at The Princess Caribe Deluxe hotel. Unfortunately our experience with the Tui rep, Wilson, was very poor or non existent. We never received a welcome drink upon arrival, and Wilson was nowhere to be seen.  During the rest of our stay, he was occassionaly seen in the foyer or at his desk. He was very unapproachable and made us feel that we were wasting his time. No "Tui" smile, no helpful information (only the bare minimum given). On our penultimate day, we had not received a checking out letter from the hotel or any information on our pick up time. When we asked the hotel reception staff, they informed us this was not their responsibility and that we should see our Tui rep. Wilson was again quite miserable and almost "grudgingly" looked up when our transfer bus would arrive. When asked what time the pick up was (as there was a delay) he was very dismissive and didn't bother to check for us. On our departure day, the next day, it was his day off! We were kept waiting and concerned about the transfer time due to the delays, but there was no-one we could ask. Wilson could have been a lot more helpful, he could have informed us he would not be around on our departure day but some form of contact would be available to us.We have been on many Tui holidays and the reps have been lovely and helpful and smiling. We have never met such a miserable and unapproachable rep.

The dynamic pricing isn't however what members should experience when they have already paid a fee to join the 'Club'Thanks Steve for a very highly respected understanding reply to the members issues. Thank you, hopefully you will be given a more senior role and bring the club back to its very best.The reply in question10 minutes agoHi Fiona. Thank you for your review. We do value your long-standing membership. In regards to pricing, flexible/dynamic pricing allows the Club to respond to changing circumstances - such as the recent severe increases in fuel and the cost of operating the campsite network. Any revenue surplus is reinvested back into improving the campsite network or purchasing new campsites - all for the benefit of the members. We have taken into account the feedback from our members with regards to the dynamic pricing, and last year have trialled a number of offers and promotions. We released 2 lots of free night vouchers to all members, and have a number of other offers in place, now ready for the current 2025 season. We recognise that higher costs of living are challenging many members - that’s why we’re doing everything we can to make booking a trip at one of our sites as accessible as possible, including lowering some of our site fees.Please be assured, cancellations and amendments are handled on a case by case basis so please get in touch with us directly should a cancellation or amendment need to be made.We are always looking for ways to improve our services and will take your feedback into consideration. Wishing you a lovely 2025 season - Steve, Caravan and Motorhome Club Social Media Team

title: A difficult decision but hard to justify membership
review: I have been a member for 40 years starting off with a trailer tent and progressing via caravans to motorhomes as my wife and I retired. The aspect that caused me to first reconsider renewing my membership was the fact that when the sites re-opened after Covid no extension of membership was given to compensate for the period when the sites were closed. The direction of the club has changed radically in recent years with a move away from general caravanning to a form of glamping. Paradoxically over the same period our motorhome had become more sophisticated and our site requirements have reduced. In previous years I have purchased insurance through the club and travelled with Red Pennant, however recovery is included in my insurance with Comfort. I have previously booked ferry crossings with the club, but found that changing the booking was expensive and unwieldy being limited to Monday to Friday office hours. I now book direct with the operator. As a motorhome user our usage of the sites has changed, arriving at say 16:00 and leaving at 10:00 the next morning which makes site fees approaching £40 for two adults very expensive for the time spent on site. When we first joined the alternatives were poor or non existent. However in the intervening years commercial sites are now both of an equal quality and competitive, many local councils, as well as Forestry Scotland allow parking one night in seven on a no frills basis at minimal cost. For us continued membership is too hard to justify and consequently we will not be renewing. Coincidentally we are also members of the CCC and have renewed our membership which perhaps tells its own story.

title: As a long-standing member for 35 years…
review: As a long-standing member for 35 years we find that the caravan club has lost its way , as its become more like  a profit making travel agent , insurance  company , breakdown  insurance   , shop , and many other diverse business trading under the name of the caravan and motor home club.. The camping sites offered as club members  are almost as expensive as most commercial camp sites  and no longer  affordable for ordinary pensioners like us . We still pay our yearly membership as we book ferries and insure our camper van through the club offering s.we rarely book UK sites any more as are to expensive and don't like having to book up pitches 12 months in advance in order to secure a pitch for a short break or a ferry  stop over  near Portsmouth.  The club used to be more friendly and affordable but has become an elitist organisation for those who can afford 100k motorhomes and the £40  + site fees . The sites don't allow us to arrive until 1 o'clock and we must leave by 11am a.m. latest on the next day, i.e., 21 hours ( not value for money for a 1 night  stays).  More discounts should be available for midweek stays for pensioners and discounts for ferry site  stop overs ( we arrive late and leave  6am to catch  the ferry  boats & on site for max of 10 hours put have to pay £40 for the privilege) .

title: My booking experience with Travel House UK
review: The booking happened OK but my main gripe is about the 'hidden stuff' around payments. It was £30 each time to pay with a credit card. Used debit card for deposit. For the rest, I went through hell with 4 more credit cards which refused payments - later learned that was due to apparently fraudsters target this company for scams etc. Finally , they disclosed to me that it was OK to pay via a 'Payment Link' from them that was also free to use!! It worked in 2 minutes like a dream. They also charged me £30 for using a credit card and another £35 because the payment went through following their cut off time, DUE TO THEIR OWN FAULTS!. Wrote to their Customer Services (Head) twice who still has not addressed my points after 2 months.Update on 14 May 23 -  Over 2 months elapsed since Travel House UK promised to investigate my complaint. I have not heard from them since - checked the JUNK folder as well!. Seems like It was just a 'Public Relations gesture! to fool the Review Readers that it was an isolated incident and something was being done to put things right!

title: Abandoned after booking
review: While the booking process with TravelHouse was excellent, part of the reason to use a travel agency service is to have a person who will help when travel issues occur later. I needed to revise my return plans whilst on the trip I purchased through TravelHouseUK, and for a solid week attempted to get in touch through phone calls, WhatsApp messages, emails, and the webform. One WhatsApp message was returned, indicating that an agent would be in touch shortly. He was not. The emails and web messages were ignored. For the phone calls, I was promised that an agent would return the call 'soon' or was 'on a short break.' I never received return calls. The upside of TravelHouse is that the prices are good, and the agent can be helpful when you initially book. However, I found the lack of responsiveness and evasion disconcerting -- in addition to frustrating.

title: The Company were very helpful
review: The Company itself were very helpful. However, from the time of staring to do an online reservation to checkout  the price went up by £100 due to the hotel company (Hilton) changing the pricing for dinner, bed and breakfast by the time we got to checkout .    There was no warning that this would happen. Naturally,  we believed that the advertised price would be the price.  This meant the advertised  "deal" was not such a  deal after all and we could not progress with the booking as we could not afford an extra £100 since it would have meant that dinner would have been £50 per head... far more than we would every pay anywhere (including there.. .having eaten there. only recently).   The same thing happened when we tried instead to book bed and breakfast at the advertised rate. Again the price went up significantly by checkout. The irony was that the company was recommended by Hilton for dinner, bed and breakfast when my brother stayed at the same hotel but on room and breakfast only as the hotel did not directly offer d,b.b.  If companies like HILTON can  offer a rate and then change  it  without notice  then it does nothing for customer relations  and really against the  spirit of Section 20 of the Consumer Protection Act which states (sic)........makes it a criminal offence for a person in the course of his business to give consumers a misleading price indication about goods, services, accommodation ..... The staff on the phone at my hotel break .com  were very helpful  because  our  attempt to pay failed due to our first attempt wanting a code to be sent to a phone. However because the card holder was already on the phone to me booking on their behalf on line,   (as they are not on the internet) the code number sent online lapsed so it all got very complicated. It has been drawn to my attention that some of the rates now on booking.com  are less.

title: Premier Inn: Affordable luxury
review: I am a loyal customer to Premier Inn as their affordable quality hotels are pretty much everywhere in the UK, and where there is one I will stay in it.You know check in will be quick and you know when you walk into your room you'll find a bed with a super comfy mattress, a large TV, a large desk, a bathroom with a powerful shower (some over a bath and others walk in) and free WiFi (though the free WiFi is slow). Hotels with the next gen rooms are even better as they feature a modern aesthetic and feel, as well as purple mood lighting in various areas of the room. Plus, you can sleep well knowing all the rooms have been cleaned following an enhanced cleaning process. Only problems are the extra charges: for breakfast (is worth paying extra as the buffet breakfast fills you up until at least mid afternoon) and for decent WiFi (the free WiFi can be slow and drop out at times so also worth £5 a day for short stays). Also the restaurants in the evenings, service can be hit and miss but the food is very good.

Happily recommend the Premier Inn BUT do not recommend their 'in-house' taxi company.  Make separate airport transfers.

title: PREMIER INN ABINGDON NEAR OXFORD
review: As a couple we have stayed at many premiers inns over the last few years this is definitely the most disappointing, not awful but considered well below their normal high standards. The staff were good, though under resourced.1. Night before email received to say their restaurant would not be open due to 'unforeseen circumstances' no explanation given. This meant we had to travel to restaurants for our two night stay. The attraction of Premier Inn to us is having a restaurant on site.2. Check in via their new terminals, one was broken the other was not coding the key cards for our room. Eventually receptionist arrived another couple has also pressed the bell for help. Receptionist was helpful and understood these machines were causing issues.3. Room OK well kitted out, however one ceiling tile partially hanging down by entrance door, room down side of bed next to shower room very narrow.4. Very limited breakfast next morning, only bacon, mushrooms, baked beans and fried egg. Eggs were rubbery, bacon very hard. No orange juice or brown bread for toast. Well below standards expected felt very poor value for money. Next day normal service resumed fried eggs though still rubbery. 5. The right hand lift was out of action for our whole stay Sunday to Tuesday. No sign on lift to indicate the problem.We will not be staying at this site ever again, hopefully their internal inspectors will review my comments and take action.

title: Be aware that Premier Inn’s ‘Good Night’s Sleep Guarantee’ is not guaranteed
review: Leeds East Premier InnSpent a couple of nights at the hotel. Staff were very welcoming and helpful. The room was clean and spacious, if a little dated. The first night was unproblematic. However, on the second night, we heard noises from the room above which went on for several hours and got worse and worse. By 4 a.m. when I was considering going along to reception, it was starting to calm down and we managed to get some sleep.When we mentioned it the following morning to reception, we received an apology and were advised that there had already been a number of other complaints about it. Apparently it was a wedding party.On phoning the telephone number provided in order to claim under Premier Inn’s ‘A Good Night’s Sleep Guarantee’ we were advised that we should have contacted reception at the time and that we were, therefore, not eligible. I found this very disappointing especially given the fact that we were not the only ones to complain, which supported our claim about the level and extent of the disturbance. A word of warning to anyone who finds themselves in a similar situation - complain to reception immediately.

description: We're the UK and Ireland's largest and fastest growing hotel chain. With over 600 hotels,you can find a good night's sleep everywhere.
title: The Ryanair of Hotels
review: Our first stay, not terribly impressed.We've stayed in many hotels all over the world and I kind of expected better from Premier Inn. I know it's no frills but I assumed they'd be on a par with or better than the likes of Travel Lodge or Holiday Inn. The room is fine, if a little dated.But you don't feel like the standards of anything are above and beyond.The thing that really disappoints is that, like Ryanair, everything is charged extra. Want to park your car? Extra.Wifi is free but unusable.. would you like it quicker than a snail? Extra. Want breakfast? Extra. On top of that:The reception staff didn't exactly look pleased to see us. They seem bored and unmotivated. The TV in the room, whilst apparently 'smart' isn't really smart. No apps, no connectivity. No USB sockets in the room.The walls and skirting could do with a clean and a paint. The wall next to the bed is covered in drips from spilt drinks and other scuffs, stains and scrapes. It's obviously not regularly taken care of. The bar and lounge is completely soulless, not inviting at all. I would definitely think twice before reluctantly staying in a Premier Inn again. Three stars, because it wasn't awful but it didn't shine.

title: We got a very good holiday in the end
review: My wife booked a budget one week holiday with Super Escapes. The day after booking, on reading some bad reviews of the Company, especially, that holidays booked with SE were subject to unwanted changes, such as flight times and airports, and even the holiday venues. We decided to cancel with them, only to find that because it was a package holiday, we could be liable for more than the holiday cost. In the end, we were offered a better hotel, with transfers included, to a different but equally good location, from the same airport and with more convenient flight times. However, communication from this Company leaves a lot to be desired. Despite repeated requests for invoices, receipts and clarifications, we had to ring numerous times to get things finalised. Having said that, the various customer service operatives were at times very patient and helpful, especially Rio and Selina and the holiday itself was very good value and went without a hitch. Despite the communication issues, the phones were answered quickly, with only a short wait, although frequently with long, silent, holds between operatives.

title: Spacious house located in wonderful grounds
review: Wellbrook Place is located in a wonderful, rural setting with well maintained grounds.The house felt large and roomy even for our party of 20 people. The kitchen/dining room was sufficiently large to host such numbers that there was no sense of being cramped. There were endless glasses, plates, cooking pans etc. that the only difficulty was remembering which cupboard to look in!The bedrooms were all spacious and comfortable - bar one on the ground floor which was rather pokey.Looking at negatives, the house itself could benefit from a bit of TLC. For example, walking in via the front door, one immediately notices a rather dirty carpet. And in the adjoining coach house, there's a lingering odour of damp. There were minor issues too such as one of the fridges badly needed to be defrosted; insufficient tea towels had been provided (rectified quickly by the managers) and one of the bathroom soap dispensers had failed to be refilled.However, all in all, we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves and would hire the venue again.

title: Milton House: once fine; slightly neglected

Group Retreats were helpful with my booking and accommodating of extra requests. However, the maintenance of Milton House was a little lacking. The locks on the bathroom doors were broken, so my guests had to use their initiative to preserve their privacy; the tennis court was surrounded by thistles; the steps covered in weeds; the pianos all knackered and out of tune; my guests struggled to get through the pin code on the access gate. For the sake of a little investment and effort, it could have been a 5 star experience, and I don’t buy the excuse of small children playing the pianos causing the poor quality or lack of time to maintain the outside being due to guest usage. Someone needs to take more pride and attention to detail to preserve what could be a magnificent guest house.

title: Bad response when things go wrong
review: I’ll start by saying I’ve never before left a negative online review for anything in my life. The house was perfectly ok, but on arrival with ingredients for a roast dinner for 12 people we found there was only one single oven as the Aga was not on. We contracted maintenance who said it was out of order so we got on and did our best with what we had available. All was fine. The following day the maintenance man arrived and took hours getting the Aga on - creating a burning oil smell the whole time. I’ll point out that we were only booked for two nights and after the first evening we were planning a salad lunch and then a BBQ so had no need for the Aga to be on and hadn’t asked for him to come and do this - being in the kitchen whilst we had breakfast and made lunch. At the same time a hot tub cleaning man turned up and emptied the hot tub to clean it which took hours. It was then cold. This was our one day at the property and the hot tub we had wanted and had paid for was out of action and there was a man in the garden with us. The response from Group Retreats was that “This maintenance was in place to ensure the hot tub water was clear for you and the guests to use.” So they planned a hot tub clean on the one day we were there for our benefit - meaning we couldn’t use it?!They also said the Aga maintenance man “arrived to try and get this up and running again for you which then in turn created the burning oil smell you mentioned.” We didn’t ask or need this. Group Retreats don’t seem to realise how invasive it is having two men on the property for the one day you are there. The property wasn’t a base to go and do things - the property was the day’s entertainment, the hot tub, the food, the tennis court (where there were builders putting in a swimming pool).I wouldn’t recommend Group Retreats, not just because of what went wrong (things happen and mistakes are made) but mainly because of their response - not admitting they booked a hot tub clean in error and that they should have asked about the maintenance man coming to the property. They just put it back on us. Like it was done for us.

title: Poor customer service - avoid this company.
review: We stayed for 4 nights at Timberley Farm last week and whilst we had a lovely time as a family, it is a shame that the company were not in the least bit friendly or accommodating to our large group. Before paying for our holiday, we were in a dilemma of whether or not to go as Group Retreats do not offer any refunds should lockdown restrictions prevent large groups from going. This caused tension amongst our family as some members wanted to take the risk in paying and others didn't. When I tried to email the company on Vrbo to confirm their cancellation policy, I had no response from them, just automated emails demanding payment. We were offered no level of understanding or reassurance. They made it very clear that they only cared about getting money out of us. So this was the first stress. Secondly, I received quite a rude email from the company a month before our trip, saying that they would take legal action against illegal gatherings, fine us and were monitoring the house using sound monitoring systems which measured the noise levels in the property. All very unnecessary (we were a family group, with 6 children under the age of 5) and this just added to our bad feelings. Thirdly, the company never sent us the key code to enter the property. We had to chase this up on arrival day which took two phone calls and the first man we spoke to gave us the wrong code. The house itself, which cost a lot of money, had terrible WiFi and the Apps on the TV didn't work properly. The shower upstairs leaked into the kitchen downstairs, one dishwasher didn't work, the washing machine was useless and the locks on the bathroom doors needed replacing. All a bit disappointing for a very expensive property. We have certainly stayed in more luxurious accommodation with other companies who are much more customer centred and actually care. We had a great time, but that was down to our family, and not down to Group Retreats in the slightest. They were unhelpful, rude, money grabbing and do not care at all about their customers.

Our vision is not only to provide your group with a comfortable stay, but to give you an unforgettable experience of staying in a quintessential English country home. You will discover unique settings for a family break, corporate function or a milestone celebration; which you can enjoy in your own way.

Typically, our properties are large historic listed buildings with extensive grounds and beautiful gardens. Swimming pools and spas are features in most of our places, along with games rooms packed with snooker, pool and other games. Our properties are generally in quiet, isolated locations, surrounded by countryside – perfect for exploring.

At Group Retreats we can help you plan an unforgettable trip.

title: Really disappointing and thoroughly…
review: Really disappointing and thoroughly misleading. I used FlightOffice to search for flights from the UK to Panama City and found a really great deal for a flight through KLM Royal Dutch at a price and with timings that worked perfectly. However, I could not book on line and the site said that I had to call to book. When I called to book, whilst the operative was helpful, I was held on hold for some time and given details of other route options with other airlines. I told the operative I didn't want those flights I wanted to book the KLM flight but he said the other flights were a better deal  - which they were not.  Despite making it clear to him that I only wanted to book the advertised flight with KLM he said he could not do that but it was not clear why. His English was barely comprehensible. I ended up just telling him to leave it. The skeptic in me says that this flight booking site is a scam, set up to draw you in and then lead you to more expensive or unsuitable flights.

description: Flight Office offers lowest fares on your flight ticket. Best of the hotel, car hire, travel insurance & visa on a cheap price.
title: Difficult process after website glitch.
review: I wanted to fly home to NZ from London over the Xmas/New Year period. I did a lot of research as I was on a budget and could only afford a certain price. I found that price on the Flightoffice website. After telling my family I could afford to fly home and waiting four days with that price on their website remaining the same, I booked the flights and also connecting domestic flights within NZ (through another website).Very late that night I got a phone call from Flightoffice saying that the flight didn't even exist and there was a glitch on their website, so I would have to fly the next day and pay £150 more for these new flights. I requested that they honour the price that was on their website because it was their mistake. The customer service agent was very nice and polite and after speaking to his manager informed me that he tried his best but could only drop the price £30. At this point I also found a few more cheap flights on their website so asked whether I could book on them, but they told me that those flights were also mistakes and that they would cost £400 more than they advertised. I had no choice but to book to fly the next day (on Christmas day when there's also no public transport running, so it will cost me even more for a taxi to the airport). Plus the extra £120 and the cost of changing my other domestic flights. They then told me that the new flights were booked and that I could pay the difference later, but the accounts team rudely called me the next day multiple times and told me if I didn't pay it in the next few hours that they would cancel my flights. After this whole situation I wrote a review on here and straight away I got a call from them offering me a refund of £60 and a voucher for £60. I appreciate this a lot, but it should have been offered to me straight away. They also called me multiple times a day after this to make sure I was going to alter my review.

title: Challenging encounter with Flight Office
review: Individually, the agents at Flight Office are polite. Andrew was also polite. He is the agent I booked with initially. But there were so many challenges with Flight Office. I completed purchase of my tickets on a Wednesday 22/11/2017 and I was told I would get my E-tickets 24hrs after. That 24hrs took 6 days. In the first 5 days, I never received a call from them to explain the cause of the delay. Rather, I made all the calls to chase them. In terms of customer service and follow up, I believe it's poor. I was very anxious as I needed the E-tickets to process travel documents and I was beginning to worry even more if this was a genuine purchase or not. Though the agents were polite, each day I called to find out the cause of the delay, they kept repeating I will get it in 24hrs. I had to call the airline in the afternoon of the 5th day to ask if I actually have a reservation and why it was taking an agent so long to issue their E-tickets. They confirmed my reservation and said it is the agent's responsibility to issue the tickets, unless they have purchased from a consolidation. The airline explained that if my E-tickets were not issued, they would have to release the reservation. I relaxed at this point realising it was a genuine purchase, but I was still worried because I did not want to loose the reservation and so I called Flight Office. I also sent an e-mail to them. When I called the evening of the 5th day, the manager Bob - offered me a different flight on a different Airline, which I have never used before and I had concerns with. I expressed these concerns to Bob. He assured me that it is a 5 star airline and that it is safe. I asked why the change and he explained that the flight on the original airline company was overbooked. I asked for a discount on the new airline he wanted me to use for the inconvenience over the 5 days and he said to me that they are not charging me anymore money as the flight is quite expensive, but they are giving it to me at the price I paid for with the original airline. Bob sent me the provisional booking of this new airline to go through. I, then, recalled the original airline I booked with told me I had a reservation. I called Flight office again within 10mins of the first call. Luckily, it was Andrew that picked this time. I explained what his manager - Bob said. He initially supported him until I told him I had spoken to the original airline in the afternoon. This is when Andrew - the Flight Office agent now said to me they want me to fly with original (First) airline I paid for and he will do his best to get my E-tickets. At this point, I complained to Andrew that since the payment date above, I have not heard from him and it has been his colleagues (Daniel, Glen etc) dealing with my calls and telling me my ticket will be with me within 24hrs each day I called. I said to him it would have been nice to have a follow up call over this 5 day period and someone to tell me the truth exactly what was happening between them and the original airline I booked with. Andrew apologised and said he will get back to me 8pm that night of the 5th day. He called me back approximately 8.12pm and confirmed my E-tickets were out and I will get them by 4pm the next day - day 6. Day 6 - 28/11/2017 at 4pm I did not receive any e-mails of E-tickets from Andrew nor the Flight Office. I got worried again. I thought I wait till evening. I did not hear from them as at 7pm and so I called the airline (the one I was originally booked with) to check if I actually have E-tickets or my reservations were still in place. I spoke to a member of their customer service. He was extremely helpful. He confirmed I had E-tickets and he e-mailed them to me. He also confirmed that the flights are not overbooked and that they still have spaces on the flight as at yesterday 28/11/2017. The original airline company e-mailed me my E-ticket information between 7pm and 7.30pm. I was so pleased at the excellent customer service and support from the airline's customer service. However, Andrew (Flight Office), later called me at 9.39pm (about 5.5hrs after) and tells me he has sent my E-tickets and also asked for a good review. This is approximately 2hrs after I got the information directly from the airline.I believe as a travel agent with a lot of discounts, they are good. Also, they are very polite on the phone. But they do not follow up their clients. Secondly, I am not sure why they had problems with the original airline I booked with and paid for. I also wonder if this is common across the other airlines they have discount fares with. The uncertainty it created for me and my family was unsettling and I was becoming anxious being that we are travelling for my mother's funeral. Also, I did not need a manager of Flight Office (Bob) to give me false information, knowing fully well it is possible to verify these information directly from the airline. Also, Flight office do not keep to their promise of providing E-tickets within 24hrs. However, I don't see this as an issue if only they followed up with a phone call explaining the causes of the delay. These are the reasons I have given a 3 star to Flight Office.

title: Disappointing experience and unacceptable intimidation
review: I purchased a flight ticket through this agency. Shortly after, I was contacted by a representative who informed me that the ticket I selected was no longer available at the advertised price. The alternatives offered were inferior to what I had originally chosen, and since I wasn’t satisfied with these options, I requested a refund. Unfortunately, the refund was not granted, and I was forced to settle for one of the inferior alternatives.Unhappy with the situation, I left a negative review on Trustpilot. However, this is where things took a turn for the worse. The following day, I received a call from a representative who threatened me to change my review to a positive one, or they would cancel my flight.This behavior is completely unacceptable and, in my opinion, illegal. While I acknowledge my own responsibility for not thoroughly reading the terms and conditions, the agency's actions, particularly the threats, are beyond unprofessional.I strongly advise future customers to exercise caution when dealing with this agency.

title: Good experience even when we didn't take the trip
review: I contacted Audley Travel to help in planning a trip to Milan in May.  We were contacted by Sage Waterson.  We had a video conference.  She answered all of our questions.  In the end, she came up with three plans.  These plans were great, but after really going over the plans, we decided that at our age of 78, the trip would be too much for us to handle.  We are embarrassed that we didn't think through our capabilities before we wasted Sage's time and effort.  It was our decision that we had requested a trip that we were not able to safely do.  I would use Audley travel again and would be happy to work with Sage at any time.  This is all on us and our over estimation about how we are able to travel overseas.  I recommend the agency and Sage.

title: Disappointing level of support when things go wrong & subsequent resolution
review: We went to the USA in June this year with Audley. The holiday was on the whole what we expected until we had a flight delay on our return. Due to storms in Miami our flight to Orlando was delayed and we missed our connection back to the UK. The customer support service that Audley rave about was useless and offered no help or solution. Our flights had been booked by Audley on American Airlines and Virgin Atlantic which are not linked, therefore we had no return tickets to the UK and had to pay for new tickets. All we get now are a few apologies and an offer of dinner instead of the £7000 plus additional cost we have had. Lesson learned, don't use an expensive travel agency and expect to be looked after if something goes wrong.Additional comments 10/12/2024I am pleased to say that, following a number of conversations with Client Services Executive, Chloe from Audley Travel, we have reached a very satisfactory conclusion with a full refund of the additional monies we spent. We would like to thank Chloe for looking into the issues and for advocating our case to a satisfactory resolution. She has understood our concerns and acted to provide true customer service.

We arrange trips to more than 80 destinations throughout the world and across each continent.
Whether you want to stay in simple or luxurious accommodation, have a particular passion for wildlife, art or experiencing the great outdoors, or you're planning a trip for a special occasion, we can create an itinerary to match your interests and tastes.
Why book with Audley?
 
Audley Traveller Magazine

Subscribe to our e-newsletter for the latest travel updates and inspiration. As a new subscriber, you’ll receive a copy of our latest Audley Traveller magazine.
Our specialists return to their destinations regularly, uncovering new stays and experiences to make your trips as meaningful as possible. In our latest magazine, they share their most recent travel tips and ideas, including their recommendations for a second-time trip to South Africa, Japan, and Italy. We also give you a first look at one of our newest destinations, Norway, including how to experience it through the seasons. And, you can follow Audley client Mike’s photography-focused journey through Rajasthan, India.


Fuel your wanderlust with our latest Traveller magazine
 

The world your way

What would you like to experience? The world is a big, wide-open place, and making decisions can be difficult. Covering all seven continents, let us show you how you can see the world with Audley.
How about indulging in a luxurious snorkeling experience at the Great Barrier Reef? Or perhaps embarking on a serene river cruise along the Nile or Mekong? You could even opt for a thrilling swim with marine iguanas in the Galapagos.
Start planning your next adventure with Audley
 
We are B Corp™ Certified!

We’re proud to be a Certified B Corporation™. This means that we’re part of a global community of businesses that meet high standards of social and environmental performance, transparency, and accountability.Sustainability is a part of Audley’s DNA, especially our focus on preserving and supporting the communities and environments that you visit with us. B Corp™ Certification is an important step in our journey to provide you with the most thoughtful travel experience possible. When you travel with us, you’ll have the reassurance that your investment leaves a positive impact on our people, communities, and the planet.
Find out more about sustainable travel at Audley
title: We love the format of Audley vacations
review: We love the format of Audley vacations: just my husband and me and not a bus-load of other tourists.  Our trip to the Eastern Cities of Canada was loads of fun.  Because Audley is short-staffed following the pandemic some of the details in our documents were  inaccurate but overall it was a wonderful trip.  Our first trip through Audley was to Colombia in 2019 and it was absolutely fabulous!

title: Impossible to unsubscribe from email bombardment
review: I have tried 5 times to unsubscribe....but Audley keep bombarding me with emails...several times a week. There seems to be no customer service to help. Really dissatisfied and has put me off ever travelling with them in the future.Update 11/09/23I have just received a call from Laura Robinson from the Client Service team. She was very helpful in explaining the nature of the problem and apologised on behalf of the company. I am now satisfied that my complaint has been addressed and is in the process of being fixed. I greatly appreciate the call - proper customer service. It it would have been better if it could have been fixed sooner, but better late than never.I'm now changing my rating from a 1 to a 4 star as a result of this morning's call.

title: Never disappoint!
review: I have used Audley for various holidays across the world several times now and they never disappoint. This time I wanted a safari followed by a beach break and Theresa Arachi put together a great itinerary for me, starting in Kenya in a superb camp in the Masai Mara, followed by a lovely hotel in Zanzibar. I am a solo traveller and Audley ensured I was safely looked after from arrival and then leaving after 18 days in total. Any little issues are dealt with promptly so you can get on with your holiday. (Issues with the hotel in Nairobi for 2 nights, hence not giving a 5 star review, although this wasn't down to Audley). The specialists know the countries/areas they cover well which is very helpful (Theresa had visited many of the hotels and camps herself so knew what would be more suitable for me), so I highly recommend using them wherever in the world you want to go, either as a group, pair or solo.

title: Wonderful Private Tour in Mexico
review: Our country specialist was really helpful pre-trip, and extremely responsive when we suggested itinerary changes we wanted to make, and the trip itself was fabulous - we thoroughly enjoyed it all and it fully met our expectations.  There was only one minor blip when, well ahead of time, our flight out of Mexico was reported as delayed, and our driver was unable to contact anyone at the destination agent to see if we could be booked on another flight (though in the end we did, through our own efforts, manage to get on to an earlier flight.The one thing which was a bit disappointing was that there was no follow-up post-trip, other than for a fairly bland online questionnaire.  From our experience with other tailor-made travel agents, I would have expected that Audley would want a bit more 'colour' (eg we tried one of your recommended restaurants in xxx and it's no longer that great, or the hotel in yyy was fabulous because .....).  Otherwise, though, I would recommend Audley and would certainly look to use them again.

title: Landed 6 hours ago from a safari booked…
review: Landed 6 hours ago from a safari booked with Audley travel. Our outbound flight was delayed an hour due to technical issues. My wife contacted Audley to see if there was any contingency plans. Let’s not do anything yet as we might make it. No, their incompetence department rushed into action!! The cancelled our onwards flights and rebooked them. We found this as we tried to check in. We lost our private plane flight into the game park. We’re left stranded in Johannesburg. Eventually got an 8 hour drive to the lodge. Arrived with my wife being sick from stress and travel. Spent the next two days with a migraine. They wanted us to pay for the car. Then negotiated half, then nothing. Not what you want to deal with on safari. Nothing on the private flight I paid for into the reserve. On the way home, it was all last minute as the flight out of the reserve hadn’t been booked. The transfer from the private airfield to the main airport hadn’t been booked? We survived Audley travel due to the amazing kindness of the South African people. Additional note. Audley travel have responded to us personally and have put things right. Claire Losito has been excellent in dealing with this. Wish it hadn’t happened, but it’s nice to know that your holiday experience does matter to them.

title: Usually very good, now very disappointing.
review: I have worked with Audley many times in the past. Usually they are 5 star all the way from the agents on the phone to the ground people in country. I  have merely had slight hiccups, which are to be expected.I recently used them for a trip with my husband, who  now uses a wheelchair.  I asked specifically if you can handle a wheelchair tour in Egypt.  Yes definitely the agent said.  Whenever I spoke to him I emphasized that we needed a wheelchair accessible van and accessible bedroom.  He promised me these things. neither were available for this trip.  We had to haul my husband in and of a regular van with brute strength.  We stayed in three fabulous hotels.  Only one had a handicap room available when we arrived.  We made do with what was available.In Aswan we were scheduled for several trips on a boat.  I questioned if this was possible .  The agent Assured me they would be able to do it. Wrong again.  We were there three days and only went to on museum.The rest of the people in our group had a wonderful time, but I was seriously disappointed. Usually when I return home, the country specialist arranges a call to discuss my experience. This didn’t happen for this trip. Poorly done Audley, very poorly done.

title: First time we have used Audley Travel…
review: First time we have used Audley Travel and our last! Initial contact was great and our trip was well thought out by Lucy who was our contact. Then we received an email saying she was no longer dealing with our trip and she was handing over to Hannah.The personal touch had disappeared.This was an expensive 3 week holiday to Canada and we wanted  everything to be right. Audley have local contacts in Canada who deal with queries and we found ourselves spending a lot of time on the phone to them.On arrival at our hotel in Vancouver we were put in an un refurbished room and found out this was a specific request from the Audley agent in Canada. We were moved for our second night but this is hassle you don’t need.We then moved onto the Fairmont hotel in Victoria where our booked room included breakfast but on check in Audley had not confirmed breakfast so the hotel had to contact the Audley agent and the agent had to contact Audley and finally it was sorted but on our second breakfast at the hotel we were given a different breakfast menu with little choice which the hotel said was on instruction from Audley agent / Audley.Anyone reading this will be getting bored by now but the list goes on.Audley are expensive and that’s fine if everything is as described on the itinerary but in our case it wasn’t and we regret using them.Stuart Smith

title: Pulling Teeth
review: My Wife and I spent considerable time looking at a 2 centre Holiday in Europe (same country).We researched the Country we wanted to visit forensically, candidate Airlines and associated Airports, Logistics around Transfers, areas we wanted to Visit, type/style of Accommodation, availability etcSo we had a pretty thorough itinerary with some flex on dates.We decided to invite Audley Travel to help us given their excellent reputation.Therefore, we provided a detailed brief which we felt covered all the bases.The initial e-Mail reply was encouraging the only question missing was budget.Given we’d indicated that we were seasoned Travellers we preferred Audley Travel to cost it out themselves as they might have different ideas given their vast experience so didn’t want to lead the witness.They did have a couple of reasonable and understandable questions so that was encouraging, which we answered immediately.The representative seemed to want to talk further which is some ways was fine but there was really nothing else materially to add as we had covered everything even down to what Trains we might want to catch!It was also an incredibly busy and stressful time for us hence looking to engage their Services.This Ping Pong started to become quite frustrating so we asked another specialist in the Travel industry to get involved.Within 24 hours they provided a fully costed itinerary which was first class.We thought we’d ask Audley Travel again as the representative seemed polite although unable to provide what we wanted.We hinted at a reasonable Budget, more than what we’d been quoted to be “advised” that it wouldn’t be enough for what we were looking to achieve.We’ve given the review 3 stars as we do think AT are a good business but, on this experience, they could have tried much harder especially given what we had done so in realty should be less.Bottom line their competitor showed more interest and initiative,

title: Overall good - Cuts corners
review: Overall good itinerary… all of the highlights covered. Details are often lacking — No driver from here or there. Unable to complete tours where cane user was clearly stated up front. Ie 2000 steps not accommodated for where there are stated needs. Drivers late or with multiple pickups at same time. At a wine dinner we showed up 40 min late due to over extended schedule and later when “arranged” taxi was called at 1030 pm — there was no taxi. Waited 30 min and then just walked back to hotel at 11pm - 25 min. Totally unacceptable for the price of these trips. If tui italia can’t get it done they need to find other local organizations. But overall had a great time and saw the highlights described. Would def return to the destination but would probably not use this travel agent. Too many shortcuts to save a few dollars when the price of the vacations are $$$$.

title: We paid for a 5 star holiday experience.  We didn't get it.
review: This was intended to be the trip of a lifetime - our retirement reward to a place I'd always wanted to go to, The Amalfi Coast.  We are not confident travellers and based on Trustpilot Reviews and Audley's website we felt safe trusting our trip to them and paying a premium price.  At no point did they admit to us that once we got to Italy, we would be dealing with third parties - mostly Tui and not Audley.  We would not have booked if we had known.  We booked our own flights to Naples and had the most horrendous time with threatened cancellation and a 3 hour delay.  We phoned the Duty Agent to ensure that our transfer was made aware of our circumstances.  The Duty Agent was rather off hand and said we should have called Italy direct but agreed to notify the company organising the transfer on our behalf as we were being rushed to boarding to ensure the plane could leave and land before midnight in Naples.  On arrival, weary and exhausted, we could not find our transfer.  Travellers who had paid far less and travelled with Tui were all collected.  There was no message on my phone, nothing.  We were left in Naples airport at the mercy of the touts.  We eventually got through to the ground agent, Citalia, who told us the transfer had been and gone and they couldn't find another.  When asked what we should do, they said, get a taxi and couldn't tell us what a fair price was - negotiate they said.  It was now past midnight, we were exhausted and had no option but to join a long queue where we were pestered by touts and taxi drivers who were trying to double book people to fill their seats.  We were lucky.  We were not ripped off and arrived safely at our hotel.  No thanks to Audley.  In the morning an email arrived from the duty officer telling me they hadn't been able to arrange an alternative transfer and to get a refund from the airline!  This was not an auspicious start.  Naples was a great experience, lovely hotel, excellent guide and the driver arrived on time to take us to Sorrento.  Unfortunately, the hotel in which were to spend the next 6 nights was not up to scratch.  Italy was unseasonably cold and windy and our hotel was only suitable to hot sunshine - the name Helios, says it all.  Its breakfast gazebo was freezing and windblown and the electricity failed for the hot food and toast.  The manageress was curt and mercenary when we asked for a bottle of water in the room and as for tea/coffee making facilities forget it.  There was only a tiny bar area inside - everything was outside but it was too cold to use, condemning us to our rooms which were not designed to be used that way.  The space was on the terrace, which was too cold to sit out on.  As the hotel didn't do evening food, you were always forced out to eat - a good 15 minute down the hill into town or pay £30 for a taxi!  There was no letter, as promised in the Audley booklet with all the details of your tours etc.  Both hotels looked blank when I asked for such a document.  This rather left us in the dark.   Questions we'd pre-asked and specific modifications, such as food we don't eat to not be served on one trip had clearly not been relayed thus particular experiences were not what we'd anticipated.  I want to make it clear that my lack of satisfaction is that our needs were not met and we had paid top dollar for this trip.  Audley apologised and offered us refunds for elements as well as helping us out with a last minute guide which they partially paid for.  However, they really didn't have the local knowledge they claimed - nothing was mentioned about the Easter parades which are famous in the region and which shut down the towns when they are on.  The agent had never heard of Paestum, which is World Heritage Site, when we asked to visit it as part of our itinerary, then left it off and had to be reminded.  Thus, we feel we paid for a 5 star experience and received a three star one instead.  We wouldn't use Audley again - they did not give us the bespoke experience we used them for.

title: Needlessly expensive
review: I can only write a partial review of Audley because I never got past the planning and pricing part.My initial experience with Audley was very positive, thanks to their outstanding travel consultant Alex. Alex is Audley's Spain and Portugal expert and in all my communications with her, both by email and on the phone she was upbeat, helpful and seemingly enthusiastic about customizing the tour to meet every one of our trip wishes. I will have to admit that the final customized tour she created for us was outstanding. The problem came with the price. Now I understand there is a premium to be paid for a customized tour. As with any other company, Audley has an organizational overhead and needs to make a profit. However, when that profit is more than 36% over the actual cost of the tour, I think that is excessive.   I know how much over the actual price of the tour Audley was charging because I priced the itinerary they provided independently, looking up the costs of the hotels and private tours identical to the ones that they described in their itinerary. In fact, I made sure that I rounded everything way up to make sure I gave them the benefit of the doubt. Even doing that, a trip that I could have booked on my own with just a bit of effort for $7,200 was costing me over $11,300 with Audley. Sure, we will be taking a cab rather than a private car from the train station to the hotel and back but for $4,100 less, I can certainly live with that. To make matters worse, the international flight from the US to Spain that Alex told me should could probably get me at a cheaper price through Audley contracts with the airlines, ended up being over $900 more expensive than the same flights I was able to find online in less than 10 minutes.   If you don't mind the  unnecessary personal extravagance of blowing a couple of thousand dollars for customized service then I guess Audley is for you.  I'd rather save that money and take another trip.****Addendum 10/09/2022As Audley Travel promised in their reply to my original post, a customer service manager, Lily, did reach out to me shortly afterwards to discuss my concerns. Once again, as in my experience with Alex,  my original Audley trip consultant, Lily was  extremely pleasant, patient and apparently very determined to explain the value of the Audley tour and try to work with me in any way to get the trip with them off the ground. Despite the effort, we could not arrive at a solution that would allow me to feel comfortable with the value I was getting for my money. Just as a matter of perspective,  by creating and booking an itinerary on my own, totally online, with a virtually identical itinerary to Audley's with the same hotels plus full day as opposed to the 1/2 day tours offered by Audley in all the places we planned to visit, I saved enough to pay for our two roundtrip flight fares from the U.S. to Spain in premium economy class.  In the final analysis, I was extremely impressed with the patience and apparent determination the Audley team has in creating a great trip for it's clients. Unfortunately for me, the steep premium that involves just does not make financial sense.

title: Issues with room reservations - resolved by a senior manager
review: I was promised a room at the Kasbah Tamadot in the High Atlas mts in Morocco and signed a contract.  Then 5 days later, I was told that particular room was not available, but I could upgrade for $2800 for 3 nights.  This increase is ridiculous.  I found the exact room I wanted on Trip Advisor for $1065/night, about the same as the additional money Audley wanted.  You do the math!  Next day - first I get an e-mail saying that the $2800 was incorrect, but still costing several hundred dollars more.  After a conversation with a senior manager, Audley will honor our contract at no additional cost.  I can only give 3 stars at this time because of my aggravation and frustration.

I do not think we were given the best advice for our 2 week trip, the best bits were the ones we looked into and arranged ourselves! I did not expect this from Audley travel, who claim to be experts in Vietnam, and have had no feedback to my comments made directly to them and the issues that occurred . I could not trust them again to organise any future trips, when you pay a premium you should receive better ground knowledge and service.

title: Really dissatisfied and charged £4446 for the privelage
review: Really dissatisfied with how we were treated by Audley. They were very good at pulling together and booking a £7410 tour of the Deep South USA but 6/7 weeks prior to departure my wife had an accident whereby she needed an operation for broken bones and the hospital advised she could not travel for around 16 weeks. We have a letter from the hospital to confirm. We asked for the trip to be postponed and rebooked but was told this was not possible. So we had to cancel and Audley advised that their terms applied whereby they kept £4446 of our money and refunded £2964 !! We had Virgin flights separately and they were refunded in full.I guess you only know how good a business is when these instances occur and my experience shows that I would never use Audley again…..despite the person saying to me to get back in contact next year when ready to re book….really 😆😆Since posting the review, Audley have taken my feedback seriously and I hope will be more flexible in their approach in these type of circumstances... I have been impressed with the way in which their Directors Office has dealt with my concerns.

title: Stay away from Audley Travel!!!
review: We recently booked a trip to Milan and Stresa on Lake Maggiore. We received a call from a driver who was dispatched to pick us up from the airport on the wrong night. Despite forwarding our flight information directly from United Airlines, (although we booked in April, Audley asked for it in August)  Audley had us arriving the wrong day. We were scheduled to visit the Duomo and the Last Supper on the day of arrival but that didn't happen because the tickets were sold out and we were still in the US. When we informed the agent, her response was that we "were lucky" because we could have an early morning check in rather than a normal late afternoon check in which was totally ridiculous. Jasmine then booked us on a 3 hour walking tour an hour after we arrived in Milan after having no sleep. We cancelled that excursion as well. Another excursion that was booked for later in the trip never happened. We were also told we would have global entry back into the US which wasn't true. We telephoned Jasmine upon our return to let her know about our trip. We requested a refund of one night hotel stay in Milan, tickets for the Duomo, the Last Supper, the walking tour and the driver who was sent on the wrong day. Her response was she had to speak her supervisor. After 10 days and another email from me, we finally heard back. Basically, her response was "sorry, you lose". She told us she would have to speak with a supervisor. Yesterday, 2 weeks after the trip, we spoke with a supervisor who told us she couldn't help us. Rather than spending 2 days in Milan, we were there for half a day. Although Stefani kept apologizing, I told her that I wanted to be reimbursed for the money that was paid ahead of time. Again we were told that there was nothing we could do. We've requested itemized copies of the bill so that we could provide to the insurance company and still haven't received this either. We spent in excess of $13,000 for this trip. I would absolutely NEVER EVER recommend them. They have no customer service policy. Stay Away!!

title: We were mislead
review: I was willing to pay what I thought was a very high price because I was celebrating my eightieth birthday and the ads promised trips tailored to our specific interests and planned by experts.  Our specialist assured us that all of our guides were Spanish civil war experts (my main interest in the trip), that we would have english speaking drivers on transfers and long drives between cities and that every detail would be taken care of so that the usual hassles of travel would be avoided. Finally in Barcelona, our last stop, we found our own guide and had a wonderfully informative half day tour of civil war sites. For the  first week of the trip our drivers could speak no english. Our local  representative mixed up times and pickup spots and then blamed us although we followed our printed instruction exactly.To their credit Audley investigated, apologized and returned a small portion of our cost, about the best they could do to make up for a disappointing two weeks.

title: Very poor customer service
review: Booked to go to Japan many months ahead and very excited. Unfortunately our specialist rep left and her replacement was not very efficient. She promised things, calls that never materialised. I booked with them because I suffer from anxiety and wanted all the stress taken away. Her inefficiency left me stressed before we left. Japan is wonderful by the way but not the experience I was expecting from Audley.Well this review certainly got their attention. To be fair it was very quick. Lots of apologies and a full refund on the trips we missed out on. We have now received the promised 'pack' and it's such a shame we didn't have it before we went. It is really lovely and lots of info which would have been really useful.Lots of phone calls to keep me updated on progress with compensation and a very nice little voucher for a weekend away. I think you can judge a company more by the way it handles complaints and they handled ours very well . Sad I had to complain though. On reflection I think I would book again with them

title: We planned our trip 2 years ago so…
review: We planned our trip 2 years ago so everything should have been perfect. 1- we received a copy of our itinerary 2 days before leaving. 2- We booked it 2 years in advance because we wanted to stay at Giraffe Manor and visit the elephant orphanage. When we got there, the agency never made the reservation for the elephants so it was impossible to attend, it was a great dis’s appointment. We spent one night at Giraffe Manor and the following night we had to move to a lousy hotel near by, even though there were rooms at the Giraffe Retreat that was right there and , not only it was amazing but, by the suggestion of Tom Wilkinson, the agent, we paid more than 200$ each to use the place so why did he made us book another hotel while we could have been there. Even worst, why didn’t he book us on a flight to Seychelles that same day as, as he didn’t book us the elephant orphanage we didn’t have much to do there. 3- This is the worst part, we specifically requested the Four Seasons in Seychelles, for us it was as important as staying at Giraffe Manor. When I realized we were in a completely different resort it was way too late. The one in Mahe was not bad but the one in Pralin was not what we wanted at all. It was extremely disappointing! And there was no way to contact the agent Tom Wilkinson because he was on vacation!!!!!

title: What is Audley's added value?
review: We have been on two significant holidays to South East Asia arranged by Audley with total spend of c£70,000.  In both cases there were material shortfalls in the quality of advice that Audley offered.  Specifically we were given incorrect advice about the Covid regime, one hotel recommendation showed that Audley really are not up to date with the current situation and generally communications were poor.  One pays a premium to book through Audley and for that I expect good advice and excellent communications.  They really added no value beyond what I could have achieved by booking direct.I would put this all down to experience but Audley have specifically asked us for feedback which we have given, but they really don't listen.  Not looking for anything tangible other than an acknowledgement that their service was sub standard.  We would never use them again (we have used other, cheaper and better agents) and would advise others to be certain of their true added value before committing to them.

title: Disatisfied/Satisfied
review: First of all, I used Audley to book a portion of our European trip.   I received an invoice for over $6000 for 2 hotel bookings, 2 tour excursions and a rental car for 4 days.  When I asked for a detailed invoice, I was told that they could not provide me with one due to agreement with overseas venders not wanting their rates posted.  If I am going to spend $6000 I would like to know what for.  If I had planned the trip myself and made all the reservations I could have done it for less than $4500.  I will never use Audley again for this reason.Our 1st tour in Iceland, we where not told that the location of the tour was over 3 hours away from where we were staying.  We called the Eskimo team for assistance and was told that they could not help and to call our agent.  After calling the tour vender directly, it was determined that we could not make the tour on time so we had to cancel in hopes of a refund.Our 2nd tour in Normandy France,  it was to be a private all day tour.  The tour guide was 1/2hr late.  He then expected me to do all of the driving with my car.  He finally got a car from his office.  The tour consistent of him driving us to different locations and dropping us off and he would wait in the parking lot until we returned.At the start of our booking process,  Kelsey White our travel agent was very helpful  and booked what we asked for.  She was very responsive to any questions we had.  If it was not for the refusal to give me an itemized statement I would have considered using Audley Travel again.6/29/24:  Audley Travel has been very reseptive to my complaints and did an excellent job resolving the issues.  I am quite statisfied with the end results.

All the while she provided basic care, as possible. We Michelle to be warm and friendly and extremely professional in an extremely difficult situation. All this was done while having to resolve customer requests, including room issues while balancing the emergency. I cannot commend Michelle highly enough in the way she dealt with the entire situation.
