description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Kew Bridge Travelodge.
review: Kew Bridge Travelodge.Stayed for 3 nights whilst visiting London. The lodge is close to Kew Bridge and Gardens but be aware it is a 20 mins walk to Gunnersbury - the nearest metro station.Lodge is fine - mostly clean, though carpets (especially on the corridors) were rather grotty. The room was okay and nice and quiet.We had breakfasts in the café. These were basic 'cheap-end' warmed-up things (cheap sausages, scrambled eggs, etc) but were plentiful, with cereals, cooked, yogurts etc and plenty of juice and hot drinks. The all-you-can eat option does mean you might tend to over-do it, but it did set us up for the day! The café also had free internet which is very useful as Travelodge are really mean with internet allowing only 30mins free per 24 hours (not day) elsewhere in the lodge.We have noticed that Travelodges are becoming more and more basic over the years. Gone are the sofas in rooms (with the pull-out bed for kiddies), the hairdryers, shelves for clothes and the trouser-presses of yore but also, the shower-wash and hand-liquid is now very basic - so much so that they clearly want you to bring your own! Likewise, the toilet roll is awful - ONE PLY!!! It surely can't save much money having visitors needing to use many sheets to get a decent 'wipe'?? I think this 'saving' just makes Travelodges appear money-grabbing.One final comment though is on the behaviour of some of the visitors. On two mornings at breakfast we watched two (different) families with young kids leave the breakfast table in such a state it was embarrassing. One father sat playing with his phone as his young child ripped-up slices of toast and threw bits around the table and floor. It's such a shame that these idiots cannot control their own children and clear up a little after their own mess!

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: PERTH CENTRAL
review: PERTH CENTRALMy room was clean and peaceful, the bed comfy and I had a much needed good long sleep.  The facilities were good but possible getting a bit dated, for example a shower curtain over a the bath instead of a smarter screen but tbh I'm nit picking. The only downside was the signage, the lodge  was hard to find in the dark. All in all good value and I will go back sometime.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Your experience will vary on which hotel you stay at.
review: Your experience will vary on which hotel you stay at. Most of the ones in London are good hotels where you will likely have a pleasant experience and a good night sleep. There are a few others across the country that I know of that also fall into this category such as the Bristol Central Mitchell Lane, Bristol Central and Tunbridge wells. However there are a lot more bad hotels that are poorly located (often in loud areas such as near motorways or nightclubs). They may be cheap but you'll have a horrible experience in them. Some examples of the horrible ones that I've stayed at are Brighton seafront, Cardiff central, Swansea central, Nuneaton Bedworth and Staines. My advice is always do your research on where the venue is located and what's around it. Sometimes it's just worth paying more not to stay in somewhere noisy or problematic.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: I had a comfortable stay
review: I had a comfortable stay. The staff cooked dinner for me despite being close to the restaurant's closing time, which I appreciated because I couldn't have dinner sooner. I was also allowed to take it to my room. I rested well. The only complain is that if the room is at the front, traffic can probably wake you up early in the morning.

review: *WINCANTON TRAVELODGE*Needed somewhere to stay suddenly and last minute very late at night/early morning and travelodge has 24hr reception and will allow you in at anytime which is ideal for emergency accommodation. The staff at this travelodge are extremely kind, polite, friendly and genuinely try to help and make your stay as stress free as possible. review: We recently stayed in Travelodge Penrith in Cumbria.  Staff were so helpful and went out of their way to make our stay the best they could. Plenty of top ups of tea, coffee and milk available if you need it and hairdryers available on request. The room was very clean, basic but that’s what you pay for so no problems there. I think the lady on reception was called Vanda, she was very helpful as was the receptionist that took over from her. The only drawback is there aren’t many places to eat, just a Burger King and Greggs, but the staff gave us a list of local restaurants and takeaways which was very helpful.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

review: Arrived at Bracknell Travelodge at Amen corner, had not been there for a while, but was pleasantly surprised, rooms had been updated, looks very good, really enjoyed our 3 night stay, staff very helpful, love the new shower over the bath, anti-slip coating is excellent. description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: A Nice Stay at Travelodge Pegler Way Crawley
review: I had a short stay at Travelodge Pegler Way Crawley between 23rd to 25th September, booking ref MHYO9152061457.You cannot miss the site as it is a large building located on the corner of Pegler Way and High Street. Reception:The reception area was nice and clean, spacious and well presented.My stay was pre-booked, so check-in was fairly quick and easy and made more pleasant by the polite service from Julie.Room:My double room was a good size, clean with a desk, chair and armchair in the corner.The room had a small basic LCD TV, but has no fridge.The washroom facilities were fairly clean with a toilet, sink and shower cubicle.Unlike most hotels, WIFI is only free for the first half hour but after that, there is a charge.Food:The lodge has a fairly busy menu with fish, beef chicken, grills and caters for vegetarians and more.I opted for a combi meal that featured chicken wings.It was quite disappointing as Ken left the chick and that is what you are left with, Baby Chick Wings!! far too small.The breakfast buffet is plentiful with a choice of hot food like, eggs, bacon, sausage, bread and more. You can also choose from a variety of cereals and fruit salad. Tea, coffee, fruit juices and water is also available. Parking:Ample room for parking in the hotel car-park, which is conveniently located next to the hotel. There is a height limit, so not suitable for vehicles above 2 metres.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: They have got the balance right - good accommodation at affordable prices
review: Happy to keep booking with them every time I take a trip away somewhere.  They have got the right balance between providing clean and tidy (but basic) accommodation, at a price which even low income people should find affordable.  So when I travel I use them, or Premier Inn.  Staff in Travelodge hotels are polite and friendly, and approachable if you come up against a problem (e.g. other guests making loads of noise at 2am and keeping me awake when I went to Paignton a few months ago - but this is OK, it was a one-off incident).  I will keep using Travelodge.  But, I am planning a trip to London - can anyone tell me why central London hotels (even Travelodge ones) are so expensive even outside of the main tourist season?

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

Some complaints were things that Travelodge can't control - like noise.  Travel hack - we turned on the fan on the AC and it drowned out noise.  Also, a small portable noise cancelling machine would work well also.  Will stay again and again.

review: I am surprised at the negative reviews on here.  I stayed in a Travelodge on Paignton sea front several weeks ago for a few days and it was fine (all the other Travelodge hotels I have stayed in before seemed OK too).  Staff were pleasant, room was clean and tidy, no major problems.  Only problem is that the restaurant was a little expensive.  I think it is probably a form of 'no frills' accommodation, value for money but possibly aimed more at business people than tourists.  I will book with them again because its nice to actually be able to find somewhere you can afford to stay in when you want a short break.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Lincoln City Centre:  You get what you pay for
review: Extremely convenient for Lincoln Railway Station and the High Street, albeit situated down a rather depressing road that seems to form part of the ring road.  Check-in took 10 minutes, as there was a queue of people with various queries (trying to check-in, could not log in to wi-fi, door card not working etc) and only one Front of House lady on duty - who was very polite and kept her cool and ensured she dealt with each individual in turn of arrival.  The other staff member spent the entire time talking to a guest in the dining area and provided no support at all.   I have stayed here before and checked-in straight away so must have been bad luck this time around.The room was fine.  Nothing special but not bad either.  Just somewhere to sleep.   Desk lamp didn't work, and neither did the temperature control dashboard - I have reported both of these issues to Travelodge, so hopefully they will be fixed for someone else's stay.  Bed acceptably comfortable and I did sleep very well, but I'm never sure if that's because of the bed or because I was tired after a long journey!Bathroom small but served its purpose.Logging onto the Wi-Fi, despite having a code was problematic and confusing.  I managed it by entering my email address and then clicking "forgotten password".  It then let me in once I had created a new password.   I think that this could be clarified, as I suspect it was what was causing another resident problems.In summary, it's never, ever going to be The Ritz or anything even halfway there, but for the price it's perfect if you simply want somewhere to sleep.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

review: Where do I start?Giving the rooms a new coat of paint is not a "Refurb"!I am a man of a certain size. Putting the toilet six inches from the wall does not help.What you charge per room is not worth what you get for your money!

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Cold Shower no Hot Water - Travelodge Staines
review: There was no hot water and my wife & I had to have cold showers first thing in the morning. When we spoke to reception she was very polite and apologetic and said she had forgotten to  put the water heater on, They wouldn't offer a requested partial refund and said the manager would contact us. But this never happened. why in 2024 isn't the water heater on a timer?Also the room and bathroom were in need of facelift with lifting paint and and grubby old panels

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Stayed at Bethnal Green for 2 nights
review: Stayed at Bethnal Green for 2 nights. Thought it would be ok as said it was a refurbished hotel. Very basic, nowwhere near quality of premier inn. 30 mins free WiFi only, no hand soap in dispenser, very dusty, dirty doorway into bathroom. Hsd to ask at reception for hairdryer. Confusing when we arrived as no signs in lobby to say reception on first floor, thought we had come in back entrance as lots of linen trolleys. Only a  3 minute walk from station but it was not well lit and quite scary for 3 females. £200 for 2 nights was quite expensive , had a premier in in Deptford for £60 a night 2 weeks  ago

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Burton M6 Northbound for 1 Sunday…
review: Burton M6 Northbound for 1 Sunday night. Room clean, bed comfortable, and additional supplies of tea, coffee, etc., available in reception area. The shower functioned, but lacks power.  I give the receptionist on duty when I checked in 5 stars for her helpfulness and friendly manner.  The 3 stars are about the location - and there's not much anyone can do about that. It's a very busy motorway 24 hours, 7 days a week. Having the lorry park bang opposite my bedroom was unfortunate. It's never quiet, and the headlights as they come and go penetrate every chink in and around the curtains.  It was good value, though, and I would stay there again. Also nice little M&S Food outlet in the main services area.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Premium rate phone number
review: I did not know! And was unaware when you phoned Travelodge it is a premium rate phone number.My phone has unlimited calls and text, I did not know that I would have to pay for a phone call.Due to my mental health issues with booking on line, I phoned them.It costs me .50p per minute, unaware of this.I phoned a few times to clarify booking it costs me over £40 in phone calls.BE VERY CAREFUL IF YOU NEED TO PHONE.The hotel stay was lovely, I stayed at Weston Super Mare,Worle.  Lovely hotel, friendly staff.I will never go again, I am angry about the telephone cost.It was not made clear

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Central heating inadequate
review: Most aspects of our 1-night stay in Dover were basic, adequate & as anticipated, & that was fine.However, we are both elderly & found the CH left us feeling cold throughout our short stay.  Although the setting remained at the maximum (30 degrees), the room felt very cold throughout our stay, & there was nothing we could do to warm it up.  It was a disappointment to us both.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Travelodge waterside Bath. Dirty
review: On arrival had to wait due to reception having problems with booking system for a guest, Got checked in but door card didn't work. Reception was polite and friendly. Room basic nowhere for clothes to store unlike premier inn, no lock on bathroom door, carpet dirty needs cleaning, windows dirty, no plugs next to bed for medical equipment. No air conditioning. Service in bar is very slow as one person to deal with take food to tables and serving on the bar, one member had no clue what he was doing. But they were polite. Breakfast they couldn't keep up with demand of bringing food out to refill. So in general staff polite but place needs a deep clean everywhere. It has put me off travelodge so my September trip to York as now been cancelled and booked with premier inn

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Got to the hotel travelodge to be told…
review: Got to the hotel travelodge to be told I need to pay £10 parking as it’s nothing to do with them ? Even though there’s a parking metre in their building and a big board sign saying the parking area is not theirs we need to pay then I was watched from the two front desk women to see if I was paying and looking over at me very rude and strange as travelogue didn’t mention anything on their site about parking and takes photos of their hotel with parking in it . Police turned up at this hotel and there were a few other problems but this was with guests not the hotel itself noise wise . The hotel rooms were cheap in price and worth every penny in fairness and the hotel was absolutly spotless being a cleaner and business owner of 18 years the detail cleaner and to maintain a hotel is a lot when it’s done daily so hats off to travelodge and the hard workers apart from the parking side of it in all fairness it was worth every penny !

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

Family rooms on top of ordinary rooms so had to contend with the noise of kids running back and for. It would have been much easier to put families on the ground floor. description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.

review: Kendal centre. Parking payment a nightmare to outside company. Couldn't pay to get wifi...thank goodness for a very helpful receptionist. Basic comfortable room and bed. Decaff coffee available. Meal I wanted wasn't available...seemed to be receptionists ,not a chef. Sweet over microwaved. Breakfast ...no fried egg, only scrambled. No black pudding. Orange juice a bit thick. Asked them to toast the croissant ...came back floppy and chewy. (Air fryer maybe needed?)

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Very disappointed!
review: The Manchester Didsbury Travelodge has been refurbished but it is more than disappointing.We have been regular visitors for the last 12 years but on this visit we found ourselves ‘upgraded’ which meant same double room but now with 4 beds and no space. We were offered another room which was exactly the same.The refurb has made the rooms very dark which is made worse by the overcrowding.There was a broken shelf, missing coat hangers and a broken soap dispenser.We have booked in for over 3 weeks, our second long stay this year but sadly this may be our last unless they can find us a less crowded room. It’s very sad as it’s in a great position but feels very uncomfortable

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Disturbed night sleep
review: Stayed at the Travelodge, Worthing Sea front. Great central location, reasonably priced but we had the worst night sleep ever! Ground floor room, continuous traffic and room right next to reception, door being banged most of the night with people coming and going.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Terrible
review: Stayed 2 nights at the Travelodge in Teddington. We waited 20 minutes for someone to check us in, along with 2 other groups. The girl who checked us in had to leave mopping the floor in the foyer and she was extremely stressed at having to do everything.There was no bath mat for the shower (which was tiny) and the chamber maid didn't even enter the room on Saturday morning to straighten the bed or change the towels. We also had to pay £10 for parking on top of £232 for 2 nights of the most basic accommodation.

description: Travelodge - great value accommodation at over 300 hotels throughout the UK and Ireland. Family rooms from £19 per room in England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland.
title: Disappointing.

title: To the Management of Travelodge,
review: To the Management of Travelodge,Dear Management,I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the heating conditions in the rooms of your hotels. As a regular customer who stays at your hotels on a weekly basis, I have repeatedly encountered the same issue across all locations: the rooms are not adequately heated.Specifically, the maximum temperature allowed in the rooms does not exceed 18°C, which is unacceptable during the winter. Moreover, regardless of the room size, the installed radiators are far too small to provide sufficient heat. The situation is even worse in newer hotels with air conditioning systems, which fail to deliver warmth. No matter the temperature set (even as high as 30°C), the system either blows cold air or does not work at all.Additionally, it is extremely inconvenient that the temperature drops back to 18°C every 10 minutes, requiring constant manual adjustments, which becomes tiring and frustrating.Please understand that many of your guests work all day in cold environments and expect to return to a warm and comfortable room at the end of the day. A temperature of 18°C is simply not adequate for a pleasant environment. I urge you to take steps to ensure a minimum room temperature of 22°C during the winter, either by installing adequately sized radiators or by providing functional heating systems.I trust you will address this issue seriously and take the necessary actions to improve the conditions of your accommodations.Sincerely,Dorin

title: Odd experience with price change and refund
review: Me and my brother booked flights in two separate bookings. About 30 minutes later I received a call saying the price was no longer available and we were being refunded.I was called and emailed a few times. One guy I spoke to was quite irate and had a go at me for “speaking too fast” when reading out my DOB. I spoke to another woman after that who was very polite and helpful. I was then called up about my brother’s booking (who they hadn’t been able to reach), which I thought was really odd. I appreciate they were trying to get through to him as quickly as possible, and they didn’t give away any of his information (they only confirmed when they asked me if I knew someone else who had booked a flight through TT), but I’ve never experienced that before!My brother was refunded instantly, mine took a day or so to come back.I think TT need to make it REALLY clear that they are middle-men booking tickets on your behalf, and they should only take payment once the prices and tickets are confirmed. It was a confusing experience and it makes it harder to negotiate changes with the airline when booking through a third party.Luckily we ended up getting the same price when we booked directly through the airline, so we will not be using a third-party site again. But I do appreciate the lengths they went to notify us of the cancellation and refund.

review: They always give me a competitive price, however I've never needed to contact them for anything. While it was easy to get in contact with their advisors the outcome left a lot to be desired. I did not want a new flight, I did not want to change my flight, I just wanted to get on the second leg of my flight! It's sad as I've booked with Travel Trolley many times before but unfortunately this will be my last time. They will do anything to make a few extra pennies. Good riddance travel trolley!

title: You get what you pay for.....

The rates charged by CA were very reasonable but the cars provided were relatively old, small and not very comfortable. I suspect the two are not entirely unconnected. It's worth paying more for a bigger car when doing long distances.  The staff at the airport desks were often (but not always) less than friendly and quick to try to charge for extras even if the 'package' bought included the extras. It's important to double check the bill item by item when the car is redelivered because trying to correct mistakes afterwards is a nightmare. The quoted one-way drop-off fees are crazy and local taxes and surcharges easily add another 30% on top. I would use CA again but I would pay more for a higher standard of car if doing long distances.

title: Save yourself money, get exactly what you want by booking your trip yourself
review: Our experience started well as the staff all seem friendly, and no problems until we got to Canada. We discovered that the hotels we'd been booked into weren't as we requested. When asked if we would be happy with 3 star hotels because "they are as good as 4 star", we should've said no as we were given pretty low standard hotels. They should've asked us if we'd be willing to pay more to secure 4 star hotels as we definitely would have preferred that.If you are given an itinerary that includes Clearwater or Harrison Hot Springs then you should absolutely not accept these. We cancelled our 2nd night in Clearwater as it was such a poor location and hotel that we had driven 5hrs to get to. They managed to secure a refund for us which was a positive and which paid for a much nicer location in Sun Peaks. We had asked them when our trip to Jasper was cancelled if they thought it was still worth going to Clearwater since it was such a big detour. They said it would be, it was not.For HHS, we found out that the hotel had cost £250/night so by the time we'd realised how bad the hotel was, it was too expensive for us to cancel and they just didn't respond when we messaged from the hotel. We absolutely would not have spent that much money on that hotel.We would suggest 2 nights in Vancouver, 2 nights in Whistler, 2 nights in Sun Peaks, 1 night Revelstoke, 3 nights Banff, 1 further night in Revelstoke or in Vernon, then split any further days into Vancouver or Vancouver Island. Do some research of hotels, bnbs that you like as you'll probably get cheaper and better yourself (we booked some ourselves and they were 10x better than the hotels booked for us). We should've done more research on the hotels they'd offered but kind of defeats the purpose of the agent if you can't trust what they're offering you.Beware also if they offer to get your Parks Canada pass for you and charge you more than $22(£12)/day - it's super easy to get on your road trip. We thought using a travel agent would secure us exactly what we wanted but we were disappointed and glad we'd at least booked some of it ourselves. Canada is an incredible country and we had the best time but wouldn't use CA for our next trip.

title: WHY I WILL NEVER USE CRUISE2 AGAIN
review: Start of Enquiry October, 2022We wanted to book two cruises and spoke with “the sales girl” on this matter.  The first was a cruise around South America and the second a cruise around the Far East.  Our first cruise started in March 2023 and the second had to be delayed until February 2024 as the one we wanted was booked up till then.We asked the sales girl for luxury hotels and business class flights as we were going to do this in style, the initial email exchange was even headed “Luxury”.Lisa booked us in to a hotel in Buenos Aries and Santiago (we were going to stay a few days in each city either end of the cruise) respectively for the first cruise.  The sales girl also advised that BA’s premium Economy was a far better and cheaper solution for the flights rather than go to the expense of Business Class.The second cruise was slightly opaquer as, it was further in the future and the hotels and flights were to be left until nearer the time and Cruise2 would arrange these.  Cruise2 insisted that to hold the prices we had to agree a figure for both holidays but did mention that for the second cruise there was more than enough cash in the budget for good flights and luxury hotels.About three weeks before the first holiday (South America) we had a look at the hotels which had been recommended and were really surprised to find that one of the hotels which had been chosen was still pretty devastated after the riots which had gone on in Buenos Aries a few months earlier.  Trip Adviser said best avoided, so we got back in touch with Cruise2 and asked this hotel be changed.  Cruise2 said we had to chose a different hotel ourselves and they would arrange the change.  So much for customer service! But onto the real issue, the second cruise.  Cruise2 advised us they had chosen Qatar Airways for our flights and two hotels for each end of the holiday.  The flights in themselves seemed okay but Cruise2 had recommended and purchased Economy seats for our outward and inward journeys.We contacted Cruise2 three times to discuss the choice of seats and they said “Qatar economy seats are as good, if not better, than BA Premium Economy” so I did some research and could find nothing to support that statement. But they said you’ll save money on business class which we clearly would.  Equally, by this time we were so close to the holiday to buy Business Class seats would cost a lot more.  The first flight took around 6/7 hours and the second 9 hours.  Believe me when I say the Economy seats chosen were just that - economy.  The first flight was very uncomfortable but the second of 9 hours starting 1am in the morning was just sheer torture.These economy seats on Qatar didn’t even come close to Premium.  I cannot complain to Qatar as we got exactly what was asked for by Cruise2.  When we arrived in Singapore (after 9 hours) our thoughts were we have to do this all again and I was not looking forward to it.We arrived at our hotel and were allocated our room.  We just wanted to have a shower, and get out and explore.  But, the tap on the bathroom sink was hanging off.  We had a shower, the bath would not drain, splashing around in foul water! The safe would not work.  The chair in the room was falling to bits.We complained to the hotel and were given another room. A luxury hotel chosen by Cruise2!We looked at Cruise2 complaints on their website and it said do not wait until the end of your holiday to complain, do so as soon as you notice something wrong.We did, guess what happened, NOTHING. Just long periods of no reply and prevarication.The cruise ended in Hong Kong and the only thing Cruise2 offered us was to upgrade our return flights for an additional £1,100.00 each at our expense.That was it.However, I did manage to upgrade our first flight home (the 9 hour flight) which was a joy. I certainly was not giving Cruise2 more money booked these directly.  The second flight was back to economy and with all the attendant discomforts.To summarize, Cruise2 took our money and booked us cheap flights and hotels.  Clearly they wanted to maximize their profits, and then when things got difficult because they did not follow our request at the outset they just left us high and dry, despite us complaining at the start of the holiday as per their guidelines.  Cruise2 took our money, gave us promises and then failed to meet them.We have several more cruises to do and we will never use this bunch again.I would advise all customers to be very wary of this company.  If things do go wrong you are on your own.  And just an update, despite Cruise2 sending us an email advising they were looking into the matter at more or less the start of the holiday we have heard nothing from them and that’s twenty one days after the end date of our holiday.I would think very carefully before using this bunch, we will never use them again.They offered £40.00 to remove!

title: Cruise2 don’t care
review: Booked a cruise round the Med and Adriatic. Everything was genuine so no worries there but when arriving in Rome we were told we didn’t have transfers booked. Having paid for transfers I called up and was told that Mike hadn’t included them on my package. I was advised to get a taxi to the Port (125E) and they’d refund me on return. Having wrote to them on my return (9/9/22) requesting a refund of the transfers I have just (2/3/23) received an answer from Cruise 2 cares. Surprise surprise I’m not getting a refund. Check your paperwork reflects what you’ve paid for. Cruise2 don’t care. P.S if sailing from Civitavecchia get the train from airport.

title: Booked a cruise and stay before covid…
review: Booked a cruise and stay before covid which was postponed.  Positives cruise good and hotel in San Francisco good.  Negatives they changed our hotel in vegas from New York to Tropicana.  After reading the bad reviews on trip advisor the only way they would change it was to pay a hefty supplement.   Eva the assistant was not very helpful.  Yes the hotel was bad and should not have been acceptable for a cruise package.  Also after leaving the cruise ship by 10 am they booked the flight to Las Vegas at 7pm.  What did they expect us to do.  The other negative was the 10 hour flight journey home we were put on Eurowings a low cost airline were they wanted £9 for a blanket.  You had to pay for a glass of wine and food resembled something from Ryanair.  Not good for an expensive cruise package.

title: Eager to get your booking confirmed and paid but slow at supporting you.
review: Eager to get your booking confirmed and payment from you. After sales is not so great. You wait days, upon days to have enquiries responded too. Any amendments you wish to make require the original booker to facilitate. They don't provide clarity on their prices for the modular parts that make up the booking, so its just the overall package cost. If a cruise company or Hotel drops their rates you can't compare apples with apples. In hindsight I should have booked directly with the cruise company, hotels and airlines as I would have had better flexibility and control. Its convenient and if you don't mind about price comparisons, the hotels you are booked into the flight options etc then they are acceptable. I booked over the phone and wish I had all the detail in front of me in written format and I wish I hasn't been forced to full pay for my package within 4 days of booking. I have just received my hotel vouchers and there are hidden resort costs and fees that I am expected to now pay at the hotels. Its a combined cost of around £80-90 but that information should have been provided up front. You can see that detail on Expedia before booking. Its all smoke and mirrors at Cruise2.com. Sad to say.

title: CURATE'S EGG
review: Booked a holiday with CRUISE2 to Western Canada and Alaska to celebrate a special birthday. Sadly, we were left down by their choice of accommodation in North Vancouver.Too far out from the central part of the city, nothing there.Cruise 2 did not offer to help.
